FLUORESCENCE IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION (FISH) REPORT

Patient: [redacted name]

Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Clinical History: 57-year-old female with lymphoproliferative disorder
Reason for Referral: Possible mantle cell lymphoma

TEST PERFORMED
Interphase FISH analysis for t(11;14)(q13;q32) IGH/CCND1 rearrangement

METHODOLOGY
Interphase FISH analysis was performed using a dual color dual fusion probe set (Abbott Molecular) designed to detect the t(11;14) rearrangement involving the IGH gene at 14q32 and the CCND1 gene at 11q13. This probe combination produces two fusion signals in cells harboring the t(11;14) translocation.

RESULTS
Probe Set: IGH/CCND1 Dual Color Dual Fusion
Cells Analyzed: 100 interphase nuclei
Result: NEGATIVE for IGH/CCND1 rearrangement

Signal Pattern:
- 2R2G (normal pattern): 98 cells (98%)
- Other patterns: 2 cells (2%)

Cutoff for positive result: >10% cells with fusion signals

INTERPRETATION
Interphase FISH analysis showed no evidence of the t(11;14)(q13;q32) IGH/CCND1 rearrangement in the cells examined. This translocation is found in approximately 95% of mantle cell lymphomas and results in overexpression of cyclin D1.

The absence of this rearrangement makes the diagnosis of mantle cell lymphoma less likely, though rare cases of mantle cell lymphoma without detectable t(11;14) have been reported. Clinical correlation and additional testing may be warranted based on morphologic and immunophenotypic findings.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
